steps.name: Sample structure QC and count-integrity check
caveats: Strandedness is unknown (data context). The procedure's strand inference (rseqc_infer_experiment) needs aligned reads; this dataset has only the count matrix, so the check cannot run. A wrong strand setting miscounts antisense reads of overlapping genes or drops half the reads, and sample-structure QC does not reveal it. The step records this instead of silently skipping the check.
Sample-structure QC on counts alone can catch gross problems (empty or swapped-looking samples, divergence from its group) but cannot verify per-read assignment correctness.

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: Power: with 3 replicates per group the test finds only a minority of true DE genes, most with fold change > 2; keep alpha at 0.05, do not loosen the threshold to compensate, and treat an absent gene as untested, not unchanged (R-0017@8a47). A closed-form power statement from replicate count, depth and dispersion goes into the plan/report (RNASeqPower and PROPER are absent from the pool; rule R-0162@ed74).

Counts from STAR+featureCounts carry no quantification-level bias model: a sample-specific GC-content or gene-length effect can survive between-sample normalization. cqn and EDASeq (tools of record for the correction) are absent from the package pool. The log-count-ratio-vs-GC/length diagnostic is drawn if gene IDs can be mapped to GC content and lengths; if a trend appears, state it and recommend re-quantification with a bias-aware quantifier rather than silently continuing.

With <7 replicates per condition cell, DESeq2 sets p-values of Cook's-distance outlier genes to NA rather than replacing counts; report these genes separately from independent-filtering NAs (R-0039@968d).

plan.title: Treated vs control liver DE (DESeq2 + edgeR)
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a single two-group contrast (3 treated vs 3 control liver samples, unpaired, single batch) on a 12,000-gene raw integer count matrix from STAR/featureCounts. Raw integer counts go into the count model as-is: no length correction, no pre-scaling (R-0064@92ec, R-0026@9ab1). Two user concerns shape the plan. First, strandedness was not recorded, so it is not known whether featureCounts ran with a correct strand setting; the RSeQC infer_experiment check that the procedure calls for (R-0079@6f8a) requires aligned reads, which are NOT staged (inputs are only counts.csv and metadata.csv), so the QC step does what is possible from the count matrix, records the strandedness limitation explicitly, and the report carries it — a wrong strand setting cannot be detected or repaired from counts alone. Second, low power: 3 replicates per group finds only a minority of true DE genes, mostly with large fold changes (R-0017@8a47), so the plan states expected power up front, keeps alpha at 0.05, and adds an edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness run (alternative M-0003, R-0042@54e1) reporting the intersection of the two gene sets as the high-confidence result. Steps: blind-VST sample-structure QC -> DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage and BH/independent filtering -> edgeR QL cross-check -> report.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST with PCA on top-variable genes and sample distance heatmap, plus count-integrity checks (integer counts, library sizes, zero counts, gene detection rates)
minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in at least the smallest group size (3 samples)
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; GC/length bias diagnostic from log count ratios
negative binomial GLM, design ~ condition with explicit reference level and named contrast (treated vs control)
DESeq2 Wald test on counts with Cook's distance outlier flagging
apeglm log fold change shrinkage on the treated-vs-control coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering and p-value histogram inspection

steps.description: Final report answering 'which genes differ between treated and control': methods and versions, design and thresholds, MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histogram, full gene table (unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken log2FC, lfcSE, stat, p, padj), DESeq2-vs-edgeR robustness overlap, power statement for n=3 per group, and the strandedness/count-integrity limitation with its consequences and what would resolve it.

steps.name: Report: DE gene list, diagnostics, power and strandedness caveats
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control, how robust is that list, and what do the unknown strandedness and the 3-vs-3 design mean for how much it can be trusted?

flags.message: If the strandedness of the library is unknown, infer it before the counting step, and before you trust a count table that a counter made with a strand setting. Run an inference on a sample of aligned reads against the annotation, for example the infer_experiment module of RSeQC, and record the result for every sample. A wrong strand setting counts the antisense reads of an overlapping gene, or it drops half of the reads, and the sample structure QC does not show the error.

With counts from an aligner and a counter, no bias model runs at the quantification, thus a sample-specific effect of the GC content and of the gene length can remain in the counts, and such an effect adds a difference between samples that the between-sample normalization does not remove. Draw the diagnostic: for each pair of samples, or for each sample against the median sample, plot the log ratio of the counts against the GC content of the genes and against the gene length, and report a trend. For a 3' tag library, the count does not depend on the gene length, thus plot the GC content only. Conditional quantile normalization (cqn) and the GC-content normalization of EDASeq are the tools of record for the correction, and both are absent from this pool. If the diagnostic shows a trend, state it in the plan and ask for cqn, or for a new quantification with a bias-aware quantifier such as Salmon with its GC bias model. If the diagnostic shows no trend, state the check and continue.

With two or three replicates per group, the design step states the expected power of the test before the model. The tools of record for a power and sample size calculation, RNASeqPower and PROPER, are not in the pool here. Compute the power from the closed form of the sample size in terms of the depth, the biological coefficient of variation, the fold change, and the significance level, or take the dispersion from a pilot or a public dataset of the same tissue, and state the fold change that the design can find with 80 percent power. State that a larger replicate count raises the power more than a deeper sequencing does. The statement is a caution on the plan and not a reason to loosen the threshold.

If the smallest group holds three replicates, the test has low power. Both count models find only a small share of the true differentially expressed genes, most of them with a large fold change. Interpret the result with caution, and state the power limit in the report. Keep alpha at its default value, and do not change the threshold to compensate for the small design. A gene that is not in the list is not shown to be unchanged.

steps.method: DESeq2 blind VST with PCA on top-variable genes and sample distance heatmap, plus count-integrity checks (integer counts, library sizes, zero counts, gene detection rates)
minimal pre-filter: keep genes with >=10 counts in at least the smallest group size (3 samples)
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; GC/length bias diagnostic from log count ratios
negative binomial GLM, design ~ condition with explicit reference level and named contrast (treated vs control)
DESeq2 Wald test on counts with Cook's distance outlier flagging
apeglm log fold change shrinkage on the treated-vs-control coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 with DESeq2 independent filtering and p-value histogram inspection
